about.title: Why DecisionGuard exists.
about.intro: Important decisions are often made on assumptions nobody wrote down. We are building the tool that puts them on the table before it is too late.

p: DecisionGuard examines a business decision from several angles at once: finance, strategy, law, cybersecurity, people, operations and scenarios. The result is a clear file: the risks, how likely they are, their impact, what to check and what would reduce them.
An estimate is never presented as a fact. Scores are calculated reproducibly, not improvised by the AI. Each company's data stays separate. And the platform recommends: you always decide.
Companies of every size, in Europe and Africa, making decisions where a mistake is expensive: entering a new country, investing, changing vendors, reorganising.
DecisionGuard is in its pilot phase. We are opening it to a first group of companies to improve it with them, on real decisions.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: What we collect, why, where it is stored, for how long, and how to exercise your rights.

p: The publisher of this site, identified in the legal notice. For any question about your data, use the contact form.
Account: name, e-mail address, password (stored only as a hash, never in clear), language.
Organisation: name, country, currency, members and their roles.
Security: log of sensitive actions (sign-ins, invitations, role changes) with IP address and browser.
Contact: the information you enter in the contact form.

To provide the service and your workspace (performance of the contract), to protect accounts and detect abuse (legitimate interest), and to send necessary e-mails: address confirmation, invitations, password resets. No data is sold or used for advertising.
Database: Supabase, Paris region (European Union).
Application: Vercel, functions running in the Paris region. Vercel is a US company; any transfers are covered by the European Commission's standard contractual clauses.
E-mails: Brevo (France).
When AI analysis is switched on, the providers used will be listed here before going live.

Accounts and organisations are kept as long as they exist. Sessions expire after 14 days. Links sent by e-mail are single-use and expire after 1 hour (password), 48 hours (confirmation) or 7 days (invitation). The security log is kept for the lifetime of the organisation.

The site only uses strictly necessary cookies: dg_session (sign-in, 14 days), dg_csrf (protection against forged requests, 14 days) and dg_locale (chosen language, 1 year). No advertising or analytics cookies, which is why no consent banner is shown.

You can ask for access to your data, correction, erasure, portability, or object to processing, through the contact form. You can also contact your country's data-protection authority (in France, the CNIL).

p: DecisionGuard helps analyse the risks of a business decision. During the pilot phase, features change and some may be unavailable or modified.

Analyses are decision support. They are not legal, financial or investment advice. Decisions and their consequences remain your responsibility. Have legal and financial matters reviewed by professionals.
You are responsible for keeping your password confidential and for actions taken from your account. Owners and administrators of an organisation manage its members and their roles.
The information you enter remains yours. We only use it to provide the service, as described in the privacy policy.
You may not use the service for illegal activities, try to access another organisation's data, or disrupt its operation.
During the pilot phase, the service is provided without any availability guarantee. To the extent permitted by law, we are not liable for decisions made on the basis of the analyses.

help.label: How to read
help.riskIndex: The dossier's overall score, 0 to 100, calculated without AI by a fixed formula from the risks raised. Under 25: low · 25 to 44: moderate · 45 to 64: high · 65 and above: critical.
help.heatmap: Each cell counts the risks with that likelihood (left to right, 1 to 5) and that impact (bottom to top, 1 to 5). The further up and right, the more severe: deal with the red cells first.
help.scenarios: The index if the agents were wrong: favourable = risks one notch less likely; median = the agents' estimate; adverse = one notch more likely; severe = more likely and more severe. A wide gap means a fragile decision.
help.breakdown: The index adds up four parts: the most severe risk (peak), the five most severe (concentration), the share of serious risks (breadth) and what you don't know (uncertainty). Each part is multiplied by its weight, then added.
help.domains: One bar per agent: its length is the most severe risk raised in that domain, out of 25. The colour follows the level: green low, yellow moderate, orange high, red critical.
help.tornado: For each domain: the index if its risks were one notch less likely (blue, left) or more likely (orange, right). The widest bar shows where acting lowers the risk most.
help.history: The index of every analysis of this dossier, in order. If the line goes down, your actions or information reduced the risk.
help.portfolio: One bubble per dossier: further right means a larger amount; higher means more risk; bigger means more risks raised. Dossiers in the top right are costly and risky.
help.levels: The number of analysed dossiers at each risk level, based on their index.
help.evidence: What the risks rest on: facts you supplied, estimates, assumptions, AI hypotheses. Many hypotheses = a thinly documented dossier. Below, the audit's opinion: supported, weak, unsupported.
help.activity: The number of analyses started each month. The horizontal line is your plan's monthly quota.
help.radar: One spoke per agent. The further a point is from the centre, the more severe that domain's worst risk. Greyed spokes are agents that did not take part.
help.finding: Likelihood (1 rare → 5 almost certain) × impact (1 negligible → 5 critical) = severity out of 25. The badge gives the basis: supplied fact, estimate, assumption or AI hypothesis. The audit says whether the risk is supported, weak or unsupported (left out of the score).
help.explainQuestion: Explain the risk “{title}” in simple terms: where it comes from, what its likelihood and impact mean, and what to do first.
